valuationInputs.name: Beta
valuationInputs.reason: 8 steps, 16 Nov 2026. (1) Business: a Sri Lankan licensed finance company (leases about 73% of lending, plus gold, microfinance and SME loans), 51.9% owned by Hatton National Bank; one sector. (2)–(3) A finance company, so no relevering: the sector's levered beta. Damodaran's emerging-markets file couldn't be opened from this run; the Financial Svcs. (Non-bank & Insurance) levered beta 0.97 (January 2026, as already used on this site, web-search extract, possibly the US file) is used. (4) Local 5-year betas from web-search extracts (pages not opened): StockAnalysis 0.82 (HNBF.N0000, 5-year); TradingView 0.96 (window not stated). Only two sources, so no proper median (0.89 if averaged). The non-voting share trades thinly (2,516 holders, 15% public float), so its own beta isn't used. (5) Higher of 0.97 and 0.89 = 0.97. (6) Within 0.3–2. (7) Into the formula by scripts/reinvestment.py. Provisional: refresh in January 2027 with Damodaran's emerging-markets file and three verified local 5-year betas.

valuationInputs.name: Cost of equity
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py (16 Nov 2026): 8.24% + 0.97 × (4.2% + 6.08%) = 18.2%, ±1.5 points. Within the 12–22% house range.

valuationInputs.name: Growth check
valuationInputs.value: Assumed 8% / 12% / 16%; supported 20.0% (share of profit kept × ROE, FY 2025/26: 100% × 19.96%). All within 2 pts.
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py; earnings growth for the five years after 2026/27. Supported growth is flattered by the merger tax credit (about 17.3% without it), still above every scenario.

valuationInputs.name: Long-run ROE (price to book)
valuationInputs.reason: 20.0% in 2025/26 (about 17.3% without the tax credit), 16.9% in H1 2026/27 at a 45% tax rate; −9.4% to 11.6% from 2019/20 to 2024/25. Base assumes the leasing boom fades and impairments normalise.

valuationInputs.name: ROE path (residual income)
valuationInputs.reason: Over ten years from about 17% today, then the excess return grows at the long-run rate. No dividend for three years (capital is thin), then 1 − growth ÷ ROE.

valuationInputs.name: Long-term growth
valuationInputs.reason: Below the 12.24% bond yield and the cost of equity; needs 39–42% of profit kept (growth ÷ ROE).

valuationInputs.name: 2026/27 EPS × P/E
valuationInputs.reason: H1 EPS Rs 0.38; TTM Rs 0.78 on 2,539.6mn shares; calculator run-rate Rs 0.84 (Q1 × 4 on pre-rights shares). Base −6%; bear −15.5% for impairments rising as the 2025/26 lease book seasons. P/Es equal the justified P/Es at each cost of equity.
